title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is working on the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower. He uses fundamental groupoids with several base points (a set I of base points, e.g. tangential ones on M_{0,3}). He asks when an action Θ of Γ (an outer action of the Galois group, viewed as an action on a profinite groupoid) can be lifted from Π_1(M_{0,3},I) to the groupoid of a cover C → M_{0,3}. He also asks when that lift descends to X.

The lemma begun on the previous page reads, in modern terms, as follows.

Setup. Let u: C' → C be a functor between connected groupoids that is injective on vertex groups. Then u factors canonically as C' → \tilde C' → C.
- \tilde C' → C is a genuine covering of groupoids.
- C' → \tilde C' is fully faithful.
- Concretely, the objects of \tilde C' over x ∈ Ob C are the connected components of the homotopy fibre of C' → C. This is the comprehensive (final functor / covering) factorisation for groupoids.

If Ob C' → Ob C is injective, C' becomes a full subgroupoid of the finite covering \tilde C of C. Since C' is connected, C' ⊂ \tilde C is an equivalence.

Lifting criterion. Fix x_0' ∈ Ob C' with image x_0, and write π_0 := π_1(C,x_0). An automorphism Θ of C fixing x_0 amounts to two pieces of data:
- an automorphism of π_0;
- for each other object x_i, an automorphism of the right π_0-torsor H_{x_i,x_0} = Hom_C(x_0,x_i) that is semilinear with respect to Θ on π_0.

Let π_0' = π_1(\tilde C,x_0') ⊂ π_0. Then Θ lifts to an automorphism of \tilde C fixing x_0' if and only if π_0' is Θ-stable. The lift is then unique and is given on fibres by formula (45):

Ob \tilde C_{x_i} = H_{x_i,x_0} ∧^{π_0} π_0/π_0'.

Here π_0/π_0' is the set of right cosets with its π_0-action, and Θ acts on the contracted product by transport of structure.

The next page adds two points:
- Compatibility with C' ⊂ \tilde C additionally requires Ob C' to be stable under the lifted action.
- Without a fixed lift point, lifts correspond to Θ-semilinear bijections of the homogeneous π_0-set E_0 = \tilde C_{x_0}. Such a bijection is determined by the image of one point.

This is the groupoid version of the Galois correspondence and of the lifting criterion for automorphisms to covers, written in torsor language.
errors: Minor imprecision: the vertices of \tilde C' are π_0 of the (homotopy/comma) fibres of C' → C, written loosely as 'π_0 des fibres'.
The notation π_0 for π_1(C,x_0) clashes with connected components; this is only notational.

ideas.what: Canonical factorisation of a π_1-injective functor of connected groupoids through a genuine covering, with fully faithful first factor
ideas.modern_name: comprehensive factorisation / (final, covering) factorisation for groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Street–Walters (1973) for categories; groupoid covering theory of R. Brown, P.J. Higgins
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V treats Galois categories and fundamental groupoids, but not this explicit lemma

ideas.what: An automorphism of a covering's base lifts (uniquely, fixing a point) iff the subgroup corresponding to the covering is stable; fibres are described as a contracted product H ∧^{π_0} π_0/π_0'
ideas.modern_name: lifting criterion / Galois correspondence for coverings of groupoids, equivariant version
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (Galois theory of coverings, torsors); used implicitly in Esquisse d'un programme

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine technical lemma in covering theory for groupoids, needed for lifting the Galois action to fundamental groupoids of covers with multiple base points. It is standard material, though written out carefully.
transcription_corrections: The equation number at the top is likely (44), not (45); (45) is the formula at the bottom.
'\mathcal{T}^*' in the margin note should be \mathcal{C} ('π_0 des fibres de C' → C').

Line reads roughly 'Supposons [de plus que] C' → C soit injectif [sur les objets], de sorte qu'on peut identifier C' à un sous-groupoïde plein de \tilde C', équivalent à \tilde C' par l'inclusion, où \tilde C est un revêt. fini de C'.
'π_1(C,x_0) =def π_0' (not 'π_0(x_0)'); the defined symbol is π_0.
'on se donne un automorphisme de π_1...' rather than 'on se donne un sommet de \tilde C'.
'stable par Θ' after 'π_1(\tilde C,x_0') ↪ π_1(C,x_0)=π_0, soit'.
